cls: Selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) - trans-isomer of clomifene
quick: Investigational/off-label: typically 12.5-25 mg once daily (male secondary hypogonadism)
May be taken with or without food
Not for use in pregnancy; contraindicated
Avoid in significant hepatic disease; limited data
Total/free testosterone, LH, FSH, semen analysis, visual symptoms
summary: Enclomiphene is the trans (zu) isomer of clomifene, a selective estrogen receptor modulator that acts as an estrogen-receptor antagonist at the hypothalamus and pituitary. By blocking estrogen negative feedback it increases secretion of LH and FSH, stimulating endogenous testosterone production and spermatogenesis. It has been studied for men with secondary (hypogonadotropic) hypogonadism who wish to preserve fertility, since it raises testosterone without suppressing the testes the way exogenous testosterone does. It is not FDA-approved; this record reflects investigational/clinical-trial and off-label data plus the SERM class.
indications: Investigational/off-label: secondary (hypogonadotropic) hypogonadism in men, to raise testosterone while preserving spermatogenesis and fertility
Off-label: oligospermia/male-factor subfertility associated with low gonadotropins
Note: not an FDA-approved indication; clomifene citrate (the racemate) is approved for female anovulatory infertility

dosage.n: Trial doses used in clinical studies

dosage.d: Increase to 25 mg once daily based on testosterone response
Lowest dose maintaining target testosterone and gonadotropins
Use the approved racemate clomifene for female infertility per its labeling

dosage.n: No role and potential fetal risk

admin: Administer once daily, with or without food
Confirm secondary hypogonadism (low testosterone with low/normal LH and FSH) before use
Titrate based on serum testosterone and gonadotropin response
Stop and evaluate if visual disturbances occur
Use under specialist (endocrinology/andrology) guidance given off-label status
moa: Enclomiphene is the trans-isomer of clomifene and acts as a selective estrogen receptor modulator with predominantly antagonist activity at hypothalamic and pituitary estrogen receptors. Blocking estrogen-mediated negative feedback increases pulsatile GnRH and pituitary release of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). The rise in LH stimulates testicular Leydig cells to produce testosterone, while FSH supports spermatogenesis - raising testosterone without the testicular suppression caused by exogenous testosterone.

absolute: Active liver disease or history of liver dysfunction with clomifene
relative: Visual disturbances on prior SERM therapy

preg: Enclomiphene is contraindicated in pregnancy. There is no indication for use during pregnancy, and SERMs of this class are not used once conception has occurred. Exclude pregnancy before use in any female patient.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is not recommended; clomifene-type agents may affect lactation and there are insufficient safety data in breastfed infants.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is established and data in renal impairment are limited; use with caution and clinical monitoring.
hepatic: Avoid in significant hepatic disease. Clomifene-class agents are metabolized hepatically and have been associated with liver dysfunction; data specific to enclomiphene are limited.

moderate: Exogenous estrogens - antagonize the central effect and may blunt efficacy
Other gonadotropin-affecting agents (e.g. aromatase inhibitors, hCG) - additive/complex endocrine effects
Tamoxifen / other SERMs - overlapping estrogen-receptor activity
minor: Drugs affecting hepatic metabolism may alter exposure (limited data)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no significant food interaction described.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol; moderate intake.
interactions.diagnostics: Raises serum LH, FSH and testosterone; interpret hormone panels in this context.

rare: Ovarian enlargement / ovarian hyperstimulation (in female use of clomifene)
emergency: New or worsening visual disturbance (discontinue and evaluate)
Signs of thromboembolism (chest pain, dyspnea, limb swelling)

monitoring: Serum total and free testosterone to guide dosing
LH and FSH to confirm the gonadotropin response
Semen analysis when fertility preservation is a goal
Visual symptoms - stop the drug if they occur
Liver function and mood as clinically indicated
counsel: This is used off-label to raise your own testosterone while keeping fertility - take it once daily
Report any change in vision (blurring, spots, light sensitivity) promptly
Tell your doctor about mood changes, leg swelling or chest pain
Keep appointments for blood tests of testosterone and hormones
Do not use if pregnancy is possible; discuss contraception/fertility goals with your clinician
pk: Hormonal (LH/FSH/testosterone) rise over days to weeks of dosing
Peak plasma concentration within a few hours of an oral dose
Shorter than the zuclomifene isomer - on the order of about 10 hours (cleared faster than racemic clomifene)
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved (a New Drug Application for the brand Androxal was not approved); use in men is off-label/investigational - this record relies on clinical-trial data and the SERM class, not an FDA label
Enclomiphene is the trans-isomer of clomifene; isolating it aims to retain the estrogen-antagonist (gonadotropin-stimulating) effect with less of the estrogenic activity of the zuclomifene isomer
Advantage over exogenous testosterone: it raises endogenous testosterone while preserving spermatogenesis/fertility and the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis
Discontinue and evaluate promptly for any visual disturbance, a recognized SERM/clomifene effect
Confirm secondary (hypogonadotropic) hypogonadism with low/normal LH and FSH before use
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip it and continue the once-daily schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Specific overdose data for enclomiphene are limited. Based on the clomifene class, overdose may cause nausea, vomiting, hot flushes, visual disturbances and, in women, ovarian enlargement. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively with symptomatic care and monitoring, and discontinue the drug.
